analyzed_vuln.description: In ra_translate_keymap(), numeric values are formatted into a fixed stack buffer `char str[32]` using `snprintf(str, sizeof(str) - 1, ...)`, but the returned length `len` is used directly in `flb_sds_cat(buf, str, len)`. For large/precise numbers, snprintf returns the full would-be output length, which can exceed 31 bytes; this causes flb_sds_cat/memcpy to read past `str` (stack-buffer-overflow). The crash appears in flb_sds_cat, but the root cause is the unchecked snprintf return length in ra_translate_keymap.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer builds a msgpack map from attacker-controlled JSON and an attacker-controlled record-accessor expression, then calls flb_ra_translate(). Trigger requires the accessor to resolve to a map field whose value is converted through the FLB_RA_INT or FLB_RA_FLOAT path in ra_translate_keymap, and whose textual representation length exceeds the 32-byte local buffer capacity. Because len from snprintf is not clamped to actual bytes written, flb_sds_cat copies out-of-bounds from stack `str`.
